corpora.author: William Stein
corpora.title: Elementary Number Theory: Primes, Congruences, and Secrets

declarations.label: Stein ENT (Def 1.1.1): Divisibility of Integers
declarations.raw_statement: An integer a divides an integer b, written a | b, if there exists an integer c such that b = a * c. If a does not divide b, we write a ∤ b.

declarations.label: Stein ENT (Def 1.1.3): Greatest Common Divisor
declarations.raw_statement: The greatest common divisor of two integers a and b, not both zero, is the largest integer d such that d | a and d | b, denoted gcd(a, b).

declarations.label: Stein ENT (Thm 1.1.6): The Euclidean Algorithm
declarations.raw_statement: Let a and b be integers with b > 0. Successive division a = q_1 b + r_1, b = q_2 r_1 + r_2, ..., r_{n-1} = q_{n+1} r_n + 0 yields gcd(a, b) = r_n, the last non-zero remainder.

declarations.label: Stein ENT (Thm 1.1.8): Bézout's Identity and Extended GCD
declarations.raw_statement: For any integers a and b, there exist integers x and y such that a*x + b*y = gcd(a, b). Furthermore, gcd(a, b) is the smallest positive integer of the form a*x + b*y.

declarations.label: Stein ENT (Thm 1.1.17): Fundamental Theorem of Arithmetic
declarations.raw_statement: Every integer n > 1 can be written uniquely as a product of prime numbers n = p_1^{e_1} * p_2^{e_2} * ... * p_k^{e_k} up to the order of the factors.

declarations.label: Stein ENT (Def 2.1.1): Congruence Modulo n
declarations.raw_statement: Let n be a positive integer. Integers a and b are congruent modulo n, written a ≡ b (mod n), if n divides a - b.

declarations.label: Stein ENT (Thm 2.2.4): Chinese Remainder Theorem
declarations.raw_statement: Let m and n be coprime positive integers. For any integers a and b, there exists an integer x such that x ≡ a (mod m) and x ≡ b (mod n), unique modulo m*n.

declarations.label: Stein ENT (Def 2.3.1): Euler's Totient Function
declarations.raw_statement: Euler's phi-function phi(n) is the number of integers a such that 1 <= a <= n and gcd(a, n) = 1.

declarations.label: Stein ENT (Thm 2.3.3): Euler's Totient Theorem
declarations.raw_statement: If n is a positive integer and gcd(a, n) = 1, then a^{phi(n)} ≡ 1 (mod n).

declarations.label: Stein ENT (Thm 2.3.5): Fermat's Little Theorem
declarations.raw_statement: If p is a prime and a is an integer not divisible by p, then a^{p-1} ≡ 1 (mod p). For all integers a, a^p ≡ a (mod p).

declarations.label: Judson AATA (Def 3.1): Group Axioms
declarations.raw_statement: A group (G, *) is a set G closed under a binary operation * satisfying: (1) Associativity: (a*b)*c = a*(b*c); (2) Identity: exists e in G such that e*a = a*e = a; (3) Inverses: for all a in G, exists a^{-1} such that a*a^{-1} = a^{-1}*a = e.

declarations.label: Judson AATA (Def 3.8): Subgroup and Subgroup Criterion
declarations.raw_statement: A subset H of a group G is a subgroup, denoted H <= G, if H is closed under the operation and inverses of G, or equivalently for non-empty H: a, b in H implies a*b^{-1} in H.

declarations.label: Judson AATA (Def 4.1): Cyclic Groups and Generators
declarations.raw_statement: A group G is cyclic if there exists an element a in G such that G = <a> = {a^k : k in Z}. The element a is called a generator of G.

declarations.label: Judson AATA (Def 6.1): Left and Right Cosets
declarations.raw_statement: Let H be a subgroup of G and g in G. The left coset of H in G containing g is gH = {gh : h in H}. The right coset is Hg = {hg : h in H}.

declarations.label: Judson AATA (Thm 6.8): Lagrange's Theorem
declarations.raw_statement: Let G be a finite group and H <= G. Then the order of H divides the order of G, and |G| = [G : H] * |H|, where [G : H] is the number of distinct left cosets.

declarations.label: Judson AATA (Def 11.1): Group Homomorphism
declarations.raw_statement: A group homomorphism between groups (G, *) and (H, .) is a map f: G -> H such that f(a * b) = f(a) . f(b) for all a, b in G.

declarations.label: Judson AATA (Def 11.3): Kernel and Image
declarations.raw_statement: Let f: G -> H be a group homomorphism. The kernel of f is ker f = {g in G : f(g) = e_H}. The image is im f = {f(g) : g in G}.

declarations.label: Judson AATA (Def 10.1): Normal Subgroups
declarations.raw_statement: A subgroup N of G is a normal subgroup, denoted N <| G, if gNg^{-1} = N for all g in G, or equivalently gN = Ng for all g in G.

declarations.label: Judson AATA (Def 10.4): Factor / Quotient Group
declarations.raw_statement: If N <| G, the factor group G/N is the set of cosets {gN : g in G} equipped with well-defined coset multiplication (aN)(bN) = (ab)N.

declarations.label: Judson AATA (Thm 11.10): First Isomorphism Theorem for Groups
declarations.raw_statement: If f: G -> H is a group homomorphism, then ker f <| G and G / ker f is isomorphic to im f via the canonical map g*ker f |-> f(g).

declarations.label: Judson AATA (Def 5.1): Symmetric and Alternating Groups
declarations.raw_statement: The symmetric group S_n is the group of bijections on {1, ..., n}. The alternating group A_n is the normal subgroup of even permutations of index 2.

declarations.chapter_section: 14.2 Group Actions and the Orbit-Stabilizer Theorem
declarations.label: Judson AATA (Thm 14.11): Orbit-Stabilizer Theorem
declarations.raw_statement: Let G be a group acting on a set X. For any x in X, |Orb(x)| = [G : Stab(x)], and hence |G| = |Orb(x)| * |Stab(x)| for finite G.

declarations.label: Judson AATA (Def 16.1): Ring Axioms
declarations.raw_statement: A ring (R, +, *) is a set with two binary operations such that (R, +) is an abelian group, * is associative, and * distributes over +.

declarations.label: Judson AATA (Def 16.4): Units and Zero Divisors
declarations.raw_statement: In a ring R with unity 1, an element u in R is a unit if there exists v in R such that uv = vu = 1. A non-zero element a in R is a zero divisor if there exists non-zero b in R with ab = 0.

declarations.label: Judson AATA (Def 16.7): Integral Domain
declarations.raw_statement: An integral domain is a commutative ring with non-zero unity having no zero divisors (ab = 0 implies a = 0 or b = 0).

declarations.label: Judson AATA (Def 16.12): Ideals in a Ring
declarations.raw_statement: An ideal I of a ring R is an additive subgroup of R such that for all r in R and a in I, r*a in I and a*r in I.

declarations.label: Judson AATA (Def 16.15): Quotient Ring
declarations.raw_statement: Let I be an ideal of R. The quotient ring R/I is the set of cosets {r + I : r in R} with well-defined addition (r+I)+(s+I)=(r+s)+I and multiplication (r+I)(s+I)=rs+I.

declarations.chapter_section: 16.3 Ring Homomorphisms and First Isomorphism Theorem
declarations.label: Judson AATA (Def 16.20): Ring Homomorphism
declarations.raw_statement: A ring homomorphism phi: R -> S is a map such that phi(a + b) = phi(a) + phi(b) and phi(a * b) = phi(a) * phi(b) for all a, b in R.

declarations.label: Judson AATA (Def 16.26): Prime Ideals
declarations.raw_statement: A proper ideal P in a commutative ring R is a prime ideal if ab in P implies a in P or b in P. Equivalently, R/P is an integral domain.

declarations.label: Judson AATA (Def 16.28): Maximal Ideals
declarations.raw_statement: A proper ideal M in a commutative ring R is maximal if there is no ideal J such that M < J < R. In a commutative ring with unity, M is maximal iff R/M is a field.

declarations.label: Judson AATA (Def 17.1): Polynomial Ring R[x]
declarations.raw_statement: Let R be a commutative ring. The polynomial ring R[x] consists of formal sums sum_{i=0}^n a_i x^i with coefficients a_i in R under standard polynomial addition and multiplication.

declarations.label: Judson AATA (Def 17.10): Irreducible Polynomials and Quotient Fields
declarations.raw_statement: A non-constant polynomial p(x) in F[x] over a field F is irreducible if p(x) cannot be factored as a product of two polynomials of lower degree. If p(x) is irreducible, F[x]/(p(x)) is a field.

declarations.label: Judson AATA (Def 21.1): Field Extensions and Degree
declarations.raw_statement: A field E is an extension field of a field F, denoted E/F, if F is a subfield of E. The degree [E : F] is the dimension of E as a vector space over F.

declarations.label: Judson AATA (Thm 22.1): Structure and Uniqueness of Finite Fields
declarations.raw_statement: Every finite field has order p^n for some prime p and positive integer n, and is isomorphic to the splitting field of x^{p^n} - x over F_p. Its multiplicative group is cyclic.
